about: The dated registry of AI-slop tells. Each tell names its meter rule and its fill: what to do instead, always as a procedure, never as a named font or colour to switch to, because every published replacement becomes the next wave. Re-review every release; retire a tell when it stops predicting weak pages.

tells.fill: Set the words in one solid ink and give them presence with size, weight or space; if the line needs colour, use the brand's accent as a solid.

tells.detector: a gradient whose saturated stops are more than 60 degrees of hue apart
tells.fill: Use one flat field from the palette, or a tone step inside one hue; for depth use a real photograph or material from the business.

tells.detector: violet-indigo stops (hue 244-295) or the default indigo hexes
tells.fill: Derive the accent from the logo, the product or the place (sample it), then build its ramp in OKLCH.

tells.detector: a zero-offset coloured shadow blurred 3px or more
tells.fill: Separate surfaces with a small lightness step or a hairline; keep shadows neutral, tinted to the ground, and only for things that float (menus, dialogs).

tells.detector: a 1px border plus a shadow blurred 20px or more, repeated across a row
tells.fill: Pick one way to separate: a border, a tone step or a shadow, never two; declare it once for the site.

tells.detector: a bordered or shadowed panel inside another
tells.fill: Flatten: the inner group becomes a list, a divider or plain spacing inside the outer panel.

tells.detector: three or more small rounded icon tiles each sitting above a heading
tells.fill: Show the thing itself (a photo, a real screen, a number from the brief) or drop the icons and let a strong two-column list carry the points; vary item sizes by importance.

tells.detector: a small uppercase or widely tracked label directly before a heading
tells.fill: Make the heading say it; if a category is needed, put it in navigation or a breadcrumb.

tells.detector: more than 72% of the page's text centred
tells.fill: Align to a shared start edge; centre at most one short moment (a hero line or a closing call).

tells.detector: a face from the dated overused list, unless it is the brand's own
tells.fill: Choose the face from the brand and the user's picks: read what the picked sites use, find a family with the same structure that covers every script the site needs, and check it is not on this list.

tells.detector: one word of a headline in another family or in italic
tells.fill: Keep the headline in one voice; emphasis comes from the words, or from a line break.

tells.detector: phrases from the copy lists below, in any language listed
tells.fill: Use the business's own nouns and a concrete fact from the brief: what, for whom, where, since when.

tells.detector: two filled buttons in one section
tells.fill: One filled button per view, verb plus object; the second action becomes a text link.

tells.detector: a button or button-styled link that says only submit, learn more, click here and the like
tells.fill: Write verb plus object: what happens when it is pressed (Book a table, Get the price list).

tells.detector: text in main still invisible when scroll-triggered reveals never fire
tells.fill: Render content visible by default and animate from that state; add the hidden start state only after the script has run.

tells.detector: a number in the copy that the brief does not hold
tells.fill: Use a number from the brief's proof, or a visible placeholder such as [number of customers] for the owner to fill.

tells.detector: a blockquote or q in main whose words are not in the brief
tells.fill: Quote a real review or customer line from the brief with its source; with none, state the proof itself (the rating and where it comes from) without putting words in anyone's mouth.

en: take it to the next level
he: לקחת את העסק שלך לשלב הבא
